newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nomura chairman to take on post of president - Jiji.
newsitem.headline: Nomura chairman to take on post of president - Jiji.

text.p: The chairman of Nomura Securities Co Ltd Masashi Suzuki will also take on the post of company president after the current president resigns, Jiji news agency reported on Friday.
Nomura declined to comment on the report.
Earlier on Friday Nomura said that it would hold a news conference at 11.30 a.m. (0230 GMT) on appointing a new president.
Jiji said that Nomura would announce in the news conference that president Hideo Sakamaki would resign and that Suzuki would replace him while remaining as the company's chairman.

Nomura has been embroiled in controversy since it disclosed late last week that two of its directors made apparently illegal deals and funnelled funds to a corporate client that has been linked by Japanese media to a former "sokaiya" racketeer.

The Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC) has been investigating Nomura over the suspected illegal deals since last September and the probe is now centred on whether and how Nomura provided profits to a corporate customer, a securities industry source has told Reuters.
Jiji also said that Sakamaki would resign from Nomura's board to take responsibility for the suspected illegal deals.
Jiji and other Japanese media have said that Sakamaki would decide on whether to step down as president after the SESC completed its investigation.
SESC officials were not immediately available for comment on whether they had completed their investigation of Nomura.
On Monday Suzuki and Sakamaki both resigned from their senior positions at Japan's influential business group, the Japan Federation of Economic Organisations (Keidanren).
Suzuki also resigned as chairman of the Japan Securities Dealers' Association (JSDA) earlier this week.
